name: Act of April 15, 1874 establishing a reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfoot and River Crow in Montana
nations: Blackfeet Nation (Amskapi Piikani; Blackfoot, Blood and Piegan in the Act)
Fort Belknap Indian Community (Aaniiih or Gros Ventre)
promises: Not a treaty: Congress set apart a reservation for the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfoot, River Crow and other Indians the President might locate there, from the Dakota line west along the Missouri, up the Marias River and Birch Creek to the Rocky Mountains and north to the Canadian line (Docket 279-B, Finding 2).

This drew the south line at the Marias River and Birch Creek instead of the Sun (Medicine) River line of the executive order of July 5, 1873; Royce records that the remainder of that reserve was declared by this Act to be the reserve for these tribes (area 565).
The Act contained no agreement with the tribes and no payment for the land south of the new line.

breaches.what: The Court of Claims found that 15,289,344 acres of the land the 1855 treaty assigned to these tribes (Royce areas 399 and 574) were taken under the Act of April 15, 1874 and the executive order of August 19, 1874, and that after crediting other land added to their reservation they were deprived of 12,261,749.76 acres for which they had received no compensation.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Court of Claims, Blackfeet et al. v. United States, No. E-427 (judgment of April 8, 1935), Finding XIV, as recounted by the Indian Claims Commission, Docket 279 (1952)

source.publisher: Indian Claims Commission Decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

breaches.what: The Blackfeet Nation says that after the 1855 treaty more treaties and agreements followed, each taking huge parts of its traditional land.

landTaken: Area 565 is the land kept as reservation. The land outside it, south of the Marias and Birch Creek, was restored to the public domain by the executive order of August 19, 1874 (area 574). The Court of Claims found 15,289,344 acres of the 1855 treaty lands (areas 399 and 574) taken under this Act and that order.
compensation: The Court of Claims valued the 12,261,749.76 acres at $6,130,874.88 when taken and reduced the award to $622,465.57 by allowed offsets; no interest was allowed for the years between the taking and the judgment (Indian Claims Commission, Docket 279, 1952).
today: Royce records the area 565 reserve as divided by the agreements ratified May 1, 1888 into the Blackfeet, Fort Belknap and Fort Peck reservations (see cession-1888-05-01-indians-of-blackfoot-agency).

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's own history says that after Lame Bull's Treaty of 1855 more treaties and agreements followed, each taking huge parts of its traditional land, made when the people were not equipped to negotiate or even understand them.

openQuestions: Area 565 is the reservation this Act kept for the tribes (treaty-corrections note); the court ruling concerns the land the Act left out. The same events are recorded in cession-1873-07-05 and cession-1874-08-19.
The 1935 Court of Claims opinion (81 Ct. Cl. 101) was not opened directly; its findings are taken from the Indian Claims Commission's 1952 account of them.
The Court of Claims measured the taking from the 1855 treaty lands (Royce 399 and 574), not from the 1873 executive-order boundary.
treaties.json lists the Crow Tribe as a present-day tribe; the River Crow are named in the Act, but the Court of Claims case was brought by the Blackfeet and Gros Ventre. Not edited.
No Fort Belknap (Aaniiih and Nakoda) account of the 1874 changes was found.

plain.promised: Not a treaty. Congress set the Blackfeet, Gros Ventre and River Crow reservation north of the Marias River and Birch Creek, moving its south line north from the 1873 boundary, with no agreement and no payment.
plain.happened: In 1935 the Court of Claims found that 12,261,749.76 acres of the tribes' 1855 treaty land had been taken under this Act and an 1874 executive order without compensation.
plain.today: The court valued the land at $6,130,874.88 but offsets cut the award to $622,465.57, with no interest. The reserve was later divided into the Blackfeet, Fort Belknap and Fort Peck reservations.
